newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares absorb profit-taking, rise 0.54pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares absorb profit-taking, rise 0.54pct.

text.p: Profit-taking did not prevent Greek shares from rising 0.54 percent on Thursday but new year highs were recorded as the benchmark index clawed its way near the all-time high of 1,684.31 set nearly seven years ago.
The Athens general index settled at 1,643.51, 0.54 percent or 8.82 points higher from Wednesday's close of 1,634.69.
It opened 11 points higher and climbed as high as 1,655.49 earlier in the session before coming under heavy selling pressure.
Profit-takers swept the market at mid-session sending the benchmark index to negative territory but buying interest resurfaced to cushion the decline and sustain a climb in banks and industrials.
Industrials added 1.52 percent to their value and banks firmed 0.51 percent. Small-caps were upbeat, gaining 1.24 percent.
Market-watchers said new funds chasing stocks would continue pulling the index to higher levels in the near-term.

"The market may easily add another 10 percent to its value in the near-term. Positive corporate deals and the upcoming capital injections by a large number of listings will channel considerable new funds into the equity market in the coming months," said Vassilios Theodorou, analyst at Intersec.
Foreign institutionals were seen following the market with little impact on both sides.
